scoring: 2*argon_fit + footage(h3/m2/l1) + 1 if footage links + (6-difficulty) + confidence(h2/m1/l0) + status(lost2/mostly1/uncertain0); revived = null

games.name: Pac-Man 99
games.how_lost: Servers ended and the game was delisted Oct 8, 2023; only owners of the Mode Unlock DLC keep offline CPU modes.
games.revival_check: No revival found; offline CPU modes persist only for prior DLC owners; the 99-player online mode is gone.
games.why_interesting: Tiny arcade ruleset plus massive-multiplayer battle royale: the ideal first Argon multiplayer rebuild.

games.name: Tetris Battle (Facebook)
games.how_lost: It closed on May 31, 2019, when Tetris Online, Inc. ceased operations.
games.revival_check: No fan server found. Unofficial clones exist (e.g. Notris Foes), but no faithful remake. Flashpoint not individually verified (search budget ran out); game is server-dependent so a client archive alone would not make it playable.
games.why_interesting: A simple real-time versus game with lots of footage, a strong match for Argon's simple multiplayer.

games.name: 1 vs. 100 (Xbox Live)
games.how_lost: The game ran only as live, scheduled, server-hosted episodes, and Microsoft cancelled it after season 2 (confirmed July 2010).
games.revival_check: The Lost Media Wiki lists it as partially lost and inaccessible; a 2018 pre-release build runs only on hacked 360s or devkits and cannot host live shows; no revival server or remake found.
games.why_interesting: A massively multiplayer trivia show with avatars ('the Mob' versus 'the One') is basically a web game waiting to happen.

games.name: Outcasters
games.how_lost: A Stadia exclusive deeply tied to Stadia systems; it died with the service on Jan 18, 2023 and Splash Damage said it had no port plans.
games.revival_check: Developer confirmed no port; no reports of any return, private server or remake found.
games.why_interesting: Small-scale, stylized 8-player arena shooter with a signature curved-shot mechanic; a near-perfect browser multiplayer rebuild target.

games.name: Super Bomberman R Online
games.platform: Stadia (exclusive at launch), Switch, PS4, Xbox One, PC
games.how_lost: Konami terminated all services on Dec 1, 2022, 18 months after the console launch.
games.revival_check: No revival found; Battle 64 mode reappears as a side mode in Super Bomberman R 2 (2023), so the core mode survives in altered form.
games.why_interesting: Grid-based 64-player Bomberman is simple to rebuild and showcases browser multiplayer.

games.name: Plants vs. Zombies Adventures
games.how_lost: EA shut it down on October 12, 2014, and there is no legitimate way to play it.
games.revival_check: No revival found. One petition and one unverified 'reborn' video title. Flashpoint not individually verified (search budget ran out); game is server-dependent so a client archive alone would not make it playable.
games.why_interesting: A PvZ spinoff with no surviving way to play, and lane tower defense is ideal for a quick Three.js rebuild.

games.name: Zuma Blitz
games.how_lost: EA took the servers down on March 31, 2017, and PopCap reportedly wiped the assets with no build archived.
games.revival_check: TCRF says no build is known to have been acquired. The only revival activity is a 2018 petition. Flashpoint not individually verified (search budget ran out); game is server-dependent so a client archive alone would not make it playable.
games.why_interesting: A tiny, well-defined arcade loop with a social score race, which makes it an easy first Argon test.

games.name: Pirates of the Caribbean: Battle for Buccaneer Gold
games.how_lost: The attraction existed only at DisneyQuest and was destroyed when the building was demolished after closing on July 2, 2017.
games.revival_check: Listed as lost on the Lost Media Wiki; no home release (the Disney wiki says the digital game was never released to the public); arcade hardware, so no MAME driver or dump exists; no fan remake found.
games.why_interesting: A 4-player co-op pirate ship game, with one helmsman and three cannon gunners, is an almost perfect fit for simple browser multiplayer.

games.name: Invasion! An ExtraTERRORestrial Alien Encounter
games.how_lost: This DisneyQuest-exclusive game closed with the venue on July 2, 2017, and was never released anywhere else.
games.revival_check: Exclusive to DisneyQuest hardware; no home port, dump or emulation found; no fan remake found. Several fan-recorded full playthroughs exist.
games.why_interesting: A pilot-plus-gunners alien rescue game with full recorded playthroughs, making it a clean target for footage-driven reconstruction.

games.name: Dactyl Nightmare
games.platform: Arcade VR (Virtuality 1000CS, Amiga 3000 with custom video cards)
games.how_lost: It runs only on Virtuality pods with never-emulated custom video hardware, and only around two working machines are believed to remain.
games.revival_check: Not emulated; the SP version's CD ISO is on the Internet Archive but needs an unemulated custom card. Fan recreations exist (a Quake 3 mod, 'Polygon Nightmare VR' on Rift) but none is a faithful port.
games.why_interesting: This is the iconic first-generation VR deathmatch, with flat polygons, a pterodactyl and two players, which makes it trivially sized for a Three.js multiplayer rebuild.

games.name: Rocket Arena
games.how_lost: Delisted Nov 2023 and servers shut March 21, 2024, making the online-only game useless.
games.revival_check: No revival found in searches.
games.why_interesting: A colorful 'Smash Bros with rockets' knockback shooter that suits a stylized Three.js multiplayer rebuild.

games.name: Gears POP!
games.how_lost: Mediatonic shut the servers down on April 26, 2021, and the game became unplayable.
games.revival_check: Searched for private servers, revival projects and remakes and found none. PCGamingWiki and Delisted Games record it as delisted.
games.why_interesting: A short-round lane PvP battler with Funko-style characters, which is easy to rebuild and naturally multiplayer.

games.name: Dr. Mario World
games.how_lost: Service ended November 1, 2021, the game was delisted in early 2022, and it required Nintendo's servers.
games.revival_check: A GBAtemp revival thread found no working server. A preservation Discord reportedly holds the source code but won't release it. A 2026 trademark renewal is only speculation.
games.why_interesting: A Nintendo puzzle game with Dr. Mario rules adapted for touch, a tiny rebuild with clear versus-mode potential.

games.name: Clash Quest
games.how_lost: Supercell ended development in August 2022, delisted the game and shut its servers about six weeks later.
games.revival_check: Supercell's notice and press coverage mention no offline mode, and a private-server search found nothing.
games.why_interesting: A grid-based, turn-based Clash spin-off with simple rules, a good match for a small Three.js rebuild.

games.name: HQ Trivia
games.how_lost: After the company collapsed, the last game aired in November 2022, the app was pulled from stores in August 2023, and its servers are offline.
games.revival_check: The service briefly came back in 2020 and then died again. The app and servers are gone, and I found no revival.
games.why_interesting: A cultural phenomenon whose countdown-elimination format is very simple and naturally multiplayer, but the footage is mostly host video rather than mechanics.

games.name: Spider-Man Unlimited
games.how_lost: Gameloft ended service on March 31, 2019 when the Marvel license lapsed, and later builds need the server for progression.
games.revival_check: A fan wiki says story mode partly runs offline, but portals and rank-ups are broken. A NoSecurity blog found old v1.9 still handles currency. I found no private server.
games.why_interesting: A 3D endless runner, which is a tiny, very rebuildable mechanic, with lots of footage.

games.name: SkyClash (Hypixel)
games.how_lost: Hypixel announced removal on May 2, 2019 and removed the game on May 9, 2019 because of low player counts.
games.revival_check: Hypixel forum history threads confirm removal and that achievements moved to Legacy. I found no Hypixel re-release or community recreation, but the search budget ran out before a dedicated recreation search.
games.why_interesting: A compact island-arena PvP mode with classes and card loadouts, which is ideal for a small multiplayer Three.js rebuild.

games.name: Nintendo Badge Arcade
games.how_lost: Nintendo ended play purchases with the 3DS eShop closure in 2023 and the badge-rotation service in April 2024, leaving the game unplayable.
games.revival_check: No Pretendo support (forum threads only, and badges would need replacing for copyright reasons). The fan patch 'badge-arcade-reclawed' works only on EUR 1.3.1 with pre-shutdown SpotPass data.
games.why_interesting: Claw-machine physics minigames with Nintendo-style polish are small, self-contained and well documented on video.

games.name: Drawn to Death
games.developer: The Bartlet Jones Supernatural Detective Agency / San Diego Studio
games.how_lost: The game was online-only, and Sony closed its servers on March 25, 2019, making it unplayable.
games.revival_check: No revival or private server found (only a Wikipedia check before the search budget ran out); PS4 online is not emulated; no remake found.
games.why_interesting: David Jaffe's hand-drawn notebook arena shooter has a distinctive, low-poly-friendly art style and small 4-player maps.

games.name: Crayta
games.platform: Google Stadia, Epic Games Store, Facebook Gaming
games.how_lost: Meta shut the platform down on March 3, 2023 and user creations could not be exported.
games.revival_check: Delisted Games and the developer note creations could not be exported; no revival found.
games.why_interesting: A Roblox-like cloud creation platform with chunky low-poly minigames that fits Three.js well.

games.name: Spectre Divide
games.how_lost: The studio ran out of funding and servers shut April 17, 2025.
games.revival_check: No revival found in searches.
games.why_interesting: Its 'Duality' mechanic, controlling two bodies at once, is unique and lost.

games.name: Rush Wars
games.genre: Real-time base-attack strategy / card troop deployment
games.how_lost: Supercell ended the soft-launch beta, and its servers closed on November 30, 2019.
games.revival_check: Searched for private servers, revival projects and remakes and found none. The game was always online, so no offline APK works.
games.why_interesting: A Supercell attack-and-defend game with short top-down rounds, which fits a browser PvP rebuild well.

games.name: Clash Mini
games.how_lost: Supercell stopped development in March 2024 and shut the servers down that spring.
games.revival_check: Found a fan project called 'CM: Reborn' on Discord (status unclear, labeled soft launch) and a February 2025 YouTube video claiming a private server, plus many spammy 'private server' mod-APK sites. I couldn't confirm a working revival.
games.why_interesting: A clean 3D auto-battler on a small board, with short 1v1 and 8-player rounds that suit simple browser multiplayer.

games.name: Smash Land
games.how_lost: Supercell cancelled the soft launch in July 2015 and fully shut the game down around September 1, 2015.
games.revival_check: Searched for private servers, revival projects and remakes and found none. Online features were removed during the wind-down.
games.why_interesting: Its flick-to-bounce, pool-like combat is a very small mechanic that would work well as a fast browser PvP game.

games.name: Tetris Blitz
games.how_lost: EA retired the app on April 21, 2020 when its Tetris license expired, after which installed copies stopped working.
games.revival_check: Reports say it was unplayable even if installed. Other Tetris games exist, but this variant's power-ups and blitz mode weren't preserved, and I found no fan revival.
games.why_interesting: A paid game that was remotely killed, and an easy arcade rebuild. Tetris trademark issues mean a rebuild should be generic.

games.name: QuizUp
games.how_lost: Glu pulled the app on January 20, 2021 and turned the servers off on March 24, 2021.
games.revival_check: Its creator launched 'Sway' in 2026 as a spiritual successor, not a re-release. Imitator apps use the name, but the original hasn't come back.
games.why_interesting: Once one of the world's biggest trivia apps, with a simple 1v1 duel loop that is easy to rebuild with multiplayer.

games.name: Angry Birds Go!
games.how_lost: Rovio removed it from stores in 2019 and shut its servers down, and the game needs a server just to run.
games.revival_check: Old APKs are on Uptodown. Fan posts say multiplayer is dead on 1.7.0+ and the game depends on its servers, but I couldn't verify whether old builds still run offline.
games.why_interesting: A kart racer with one of the biggest mobile IPs, a great fit for a Three.js multiplayer racing rebuild.

games.name: Pokémon Rumble Rush
games.how_lost: The always-online app ended service on July 21, 2020, and installed copies won't play.
games.revival_check: A fan revival effort asked for help on GBAtemp in April 2026, with no working server confirmed, and there's no official re-release.
games.why_interesting: A simple one-thumb 3D brawler that a small rebuild could capture.

games.name: Ready Player Two Event Hub
games.developer: Roblox / Ready Player Two event group
games.how_lost: A YouTuber hijacked the hub with developer permissions in October 2025, and Roblox then deleted the place (Error 404).
games.revival_check: Roonby (Oct 2025) says no version remains playable. A Dec 2025 DevForum post reports an unofficial 'archive' re-upload made with saveinstance() that is missing server scripts, so it is not functionally complete. Roblox staff were reviewing it in Jan 2026. The current page at games/5607936749 shows no running servers and calls itself fan-made.
games.why_interesting: A beloved 2020 official Roblox event hub, removed very recently, with heavy YouTuber coverage. Caveat: it is a tie-in to Ernest Cline's Ready Player Two, which raises an IP issue.

games.name: Mundo Toonix (Toonix World)
games.how_lost: Cartoon Network shut the servers on June 30, 2020, and most of the game's archive was lost with them.
games.revival_check: No revival or private server found in searches. Lost Media Wiki and Lost Media Archive list it as lost or partially found. Flashpoint not individually verified (search budget ran out); game is server-dependent so a client archive alone would not make it playable.
games.why_interesting: A large Latin American kids' MMO with no revival at all, and its look is simple enough to rebuild.

games.name: Transformers Universe
games.how_lost: Jagex closed it on January 31, 2015, while it was still in beta, and deleted accounts in March 2015.
games.revival_check: No revival or private server found. It never officially launched, so no client was preserved. Flashpoint not individually verified (search budget ran out); game is server-dependent so a client archive alone would not make it playable.
games.why_interesting: A 3D browser team-arena game whose session-based multiplayer fits Argon's simple multiplayer very well.

games.name: The Sims Social
games.how_lost: EA shut it down on June 14, 2013 because too few people were playing.
games.revival_check: Targeted searches found no Sims Social emulator or fan server (FreeSO and NewSO are for The Sims Online, a different game). Flashpoint not individually verified (search budget ran out); game is server-dependent so a client archive alone would not make it playable.
games.why_interesting: A huge 2011 hit with no revival at all, and its isometric house and neighbor loop is easy to rebuild.

games.name: The Ville
games.how_lost: Zynga shut it down on June 24, 2013 after cutting its budget.
games.revival_check: No revival or preservation project found. Flashpoint not individually verified (search budget ran out); game is server-dependent so a client archive alone would not make it playable.
games.why_interesting: EA sued Zynga claiming The Ville copied The Sims Social, so the two make a natural pair.

games.name: XDefiant
games.how_lost: Ubisoft shut servers and matchmaking on June 3, 2025.
games.revival_check: Fan 'Rogue Revival' has reverse-engineered protocols but is not playable and had a takedown setback; recheck periodically.
games.why_interesting: An arcade CoD-style shooter with small maps, a good fit for a stylized browser rebuild.

games.name: Radical Heights
games.how_lost: Boss Key closed in 2018 and the early-access battle royale's servers went dark; trademark later went to Squanch Games.
games.revival_check: Fan 'Radical Heights Remake' announced discontinuation in 2022 (later conflicting update, nothing shown); no working private server found.
games.why_interesting: Cliff Bleszinski's neon game-show battle royale had a distinct look and a famously short life.

games.name: Dawngate
games.how_lost: EA cancelled it in open beta in Nov 2014, with servers kept up 90 days.
games.revival_check: Fan Dawngate Revival became 'Dreambound' with original IP (not faithful) and updates reportedly ceased in 2022.
games.why_interesting: An EA MOBA with role-flexible design, a top-down 3D game well suited to Three.js.

games.name: Boom Beach: Frontlines
games.genre: 9v9 team shooter with troops and vehicles
games.how_lost: Space Ape ended development in November 2022 and took the servers offline on January 16, 2023.
games.revival_check: Searched for private servers, revival projects and remakes and found none.
games.why_interesting: A toylike top-down team shooter that suits Argon's multiplayer focus, with plenty of alpha and launch footage.

games.name: Marvel Realm of Champions
games.how_lost: Kabam delisted the game and shut its servers down on March 31, 2022.
games.revival_check: I found no private-server project.
games.why_interesting: A short 3v3 hero-arena brawler that maps directly onto simple browser multiplayer.

games.name: TreeLands
games.how_lost: Fissy Games retired the project after a founding member died, and the listed pages show no running servers.
games.revival_check: The TreeLands (games/2228340923) and TreeLands Legacy pages are still listed but show 'no running experiences'. An uncopylocked 'TreeLands Beta Free' copy exists. Whether it is joinable today is unconfirmed.
games.why_interesting: A small original-IP tycoon that is easy to rebuild, though its lost status is shaky.

games.name: Crazy Walls (Hypixel)
games.how_lost: Removal was announced June 17, 2020 and the game was removed June 24, 2020 because of low players (about 12 on average).
games.revival_check: A March 2024 Hypixel forum thread confirms it never returned. I did not verify recreations on other servers (search budget exhausted).
games.why_interesting: A classic-era Hypixel mode with a simple ruleset (gather behind walls, walls drop, fight) that is quick to rebuild.

games.name: SimCity Social
games.how_lost: EA took it offline on June 14, 2013, less than a year after launch.
games.revival_check: No fan server or revival found. Flashpoint not individually verified (search budget ran out); game is server-dependent so a client archive alone would not make it playable.
games.why_interesting: A short-lived Maxis city builder that no one has preserved.

games.name: Aladdin's Magic Carpet Ride
games.platform: Location-based VR (DisneyQuest, HMD and motorcycle-style seat)
games.how_lost: The head-mounted-display VR ride was removed when DisneyQuest closed in 2017 and may no longer exist.
games.revival_check: The Undumped Wiki lists it as undumped and says it may no longer exist; no port or emulation found; no fan remake found.
games.why_interesting: This was Disney's pioneering 1990s VR attraction, a flight through Agrabah and the Cave of Wonders, and it maps well to a Three.js flying game.

games.name: Ride the Comix
games.how_lost: The 6-player VR attraction was removed from DisneyQuest Orlando in 2014 to make room for seating, and the Chicago venue had closed in 2001.
games.revival_check: No port, dump or emulation found. An 'Avatar View' recording survives on the Internet Archive.
games.why_interesting: A 6-player co-op sword fight inside a comic book, which suits simple multiplayer melee.

games.name: Babylon's Fall
games.how_lost: Servers shut Feb 27-28, 2023 and the always-online game, including solo play, became fully unplayable with data deleted.
games.revival_check: Searched for revival or preservation; none found.
games.why_interesting: A PlatinumGames action game that is entirely gone, with many full longplays to learn from.

games.name: PixelJunk Raiders
games.how_lost: Stadia exclusive that became unplayable when Stadia shut down in Jan 2023; Q-Games sought a publisher but no port materialized.
games.revival_check: Q-Games statement sought publishing partners; no port found as of 2025 sources; TV Tropes claims rights issues block re-release.
games.why_interesting: A modern PixelJunk game built around cloud-only State Share, now existing only as video.

games.name: Infinite Crisis
games.how_lost: Warner Bros. shut the servers on Aug 14, 2015, about six months after full launch.
games.revival_check: A GitHub emulator (EricHardiman/infinite-crisis-server) runs login, menus and Tutorial 1 only; matches are not working.
games.why_interesting: A licensed DC superhero MOBA, a recognizable IP in a format that suits Three.js.

games.name: Faunasphere
games.how_lost: Big Fish Games shut the servers on March 15, 2011, saying the cost of running it was not sustainable.
games.revival_check: No revival found. Only petitions and Facebook groups (e.g. Faunasphere Resurrection) exist. Flashpoint not individually verified (search budget ran out); game is server-dependent so a client archive alone would not make it playable.
games.why_interesting: A non-violent pet MMO that was studied academically after it closed (Consalvo & Begy, 2015).

games.name: CityVille
games.how_lost: Zynga closed it on April 30, 2015, as one of ten Facebook games it cut.
games.revival_check: A GitHub preservation project, CityVille-Reboot, exists, but I could not confirm it runs a playable server. Flashpoint not individually verified (search budget ran out); game is server-dependent so a client archive alone would not make it playable.
games.why_interesting: One of the biggest Facebook games ever, with plenty of retrospective videos.

games.name: Mighty Ducks Pinball Slam
games.how_lost: Players stood on motion platforms to steer giant projected pinballs, and the game was dismantled when DisneyQuest closed in 2017.
games.revival_check: DisneyQuest-exclusive hardware; no port, dump or remake found. Footage was not verified (the search budget ran out).
games.why_interesting: An odd competitive 'you are the pinball' arena game that would be easy to rebuild as a small multiplayer game.

games.name: Galaxian3: Attack of the Zolgear
games.platform: Theme park / arcade (Galaxian3 Theater-6 and 28-player theaters)
games.how_lost: This conversion kit for rare theater machines never got a home release, and most cabinets and the 28-player theaters were dismantled by 2000.
games.revival_check: The first mission (Project Dragoon) had a PlayStation port, and a partial, unfinished MAME driver exists (gal3). Zolgear has no home release, and a 2018 MAMEWorld post says driver work was never finished. A few Theater-6 machines survive with collectors and museums.
games.why_interesting: A 6-to-28-player shared-screen rail shooter is ideal for a browser party game.

games.name: Hyper Scape
games.how_lost: Ubisoft shut the free-to-play battle royale down on April 28, 2022.
games.revival_check: The fan project 'Scapegoat' by Fiirce has the game running offline with bots in closed alpha (February 2026). Multiplayer is not working, and the developer says it could take 'months or even years'.
games.why_interesting: Its disappearing-sector map and Twitch-vote mechanics are unique, and footage is abundant because it was built around streaming.

games.name: The Culling 2
games.how_lost: Pulled from stores with servers closed July 23, 2018, about 8 days after launch, with refunds issued.
games.revival_check: No revival found; Xaviant instead revived the original The Culling, not the sequel.
games.why_interesting: Arguably the shortest-lived online game ever, so footage is scarce and preservation is urgent.

games.name: Crucible
games.how_lost: Amazon ended development and shut all servers, including custom games, on Nov 9, 2020.
games.revival_check: No private server or revival found in searches.
games.why_interesting: Amazon's first big game, a hero shooter with PvE monsters and the 'Heart of the Hives' mode.

games.name: Warhaven
games.how_lost: Nexon shut it down April 4-5, 2024, without ever leaving early access.
games.revival_check: No revival found in searches.
games.why_interesting: A large-scale melee brawler with transformations, a short-lived For Honor alternative.

games.name: Auto Assault
games.how_lost: NCsoft shut the car-combat MMO's servers in 2007.
games.revival_check: Fan emulators (2012-2015) only reached login or entering the world; no playable server found.
games.why_interesting: A post-apocalyptic car-combat MMO; vehicle combat in open arenas is quite rebuildable.

games.name: Empires & Allies (Facebook)
games.how_lost: Zynga closed the Facebook version on June 17, 2013, and the 2015 mobile game of the same name is a different game.
games.revival_check: A fan project, Raise the Empires, uses emulators to archive and revive the Flash game. I could not verify whether it is playable. Flashpoint not individually verified (search budget ran out); game is server-dependent so a client archive alone would not make it playable.
games.why_interesting: Turn-based island combat on a grid map is a compact, rebuildable loop.

games.name: Clone Wars Adventures
games.how_lost: SOE shut it down on March 31, 2014.
games.revival_check: CWAEmu is a Unity remake in closed alpha (not public). A 'Blacksaber' private server appears in a 2023 video but I could not verify it. Flashpoint not individually verified (search budget ran out); game is server-dependent so a client archive alone would not make it playable.
games.why_interesting: A Star Wars MMO built from many small minigames, which suits piece-by-piece rebuilding.

games.name: Harry Potter: Wizards Unite
games.how_lost: Niantic shut the game down on January 31, 2022.
games.revival_check: I found no private server, emulator or fan revival project.
games.why_interesting: A major licensed AR game. Its spell-tracing encounters could be rebuilt, but the real-world map play doesn't carry over to a browser.

games.name: Disney Mirrorverse
games.how_lost: Kabam delisted the game and closed its servers on December 16, 2024.
games.revival_check: I found no revival, offline version or fan server, only fan requests for one.
games.why_interesting: Polished 3D real-time combat with redesigned Disney heroes. The gacha structure is heavy, but the combat core could be rebuilt.

games.name: Everdale
games.how_lost: Supercell shut it down on October 31, 2022. Metacore took it over in 2023, then discontinued it in September 2024 and returned the IP.
games.revival_check: I found no revival beyond Metacore's failed rescue.
games.why_interesting: A rare co-op village builder, and a Supercell game that died twice.

games.name: Hay Day Pop
games.how_lost: Supercell ended development and closed the servers on February 1, 2021.
games.revival_check: I found no revival.
games.why_interesting: A tiny match-3 game, easy to rebuild, though genre clones are common.

games.name: Vesteria
games.developer: Vesteria, Inc. (berezaa, sk3let0n, Polymorphic; Roblox Incubator)
games.how_lost: The team shut the game down in early 2020 and the official Roblox place linked from the repo now returns 404.
games.revival_check: Official Roblox place (games/2376885433) returns HTTP 404. The full source is open-sourced under Apache-2.0 on GitHub (berezaa/vesteria plus forks), but I found no running community-hosted copy. Map/asset data may need separate recovery.
games.why_interesting: A polished, well-known Roblox MMORPG whose original source code is public, so footage plus code could make for an unusually faithful rebuild.

games.name: Petpet Park
games.how_lost: It closed on September 18, 2014, after JumpStart bought Neopets, and no playable build has surfaced since.
games.revival_check: Lost Media Wiki: no playable version. Two fan efforts (Petpet Project X, Petpet Park Rebuild) are restoring cache files but have not released anything playable. Flashpoint not individually verified (search budget ran out); game is server-dependent so a client archive alone would not make it playable.
games.why_interesting: A Neopets spinoff world with a loyal fanbase, and fans are still asking for old cache files.

games.name: LEGO Legends of Chima Online
games.how_lost: Servers went offline on June 1, 2015 because of low revenue.
games.revival_check: A fan revival, LOCO Online, is reported to be in development (TV Tropes, Chima wiki), but I could not confirm a playable release. Flashpoint not individually verified (search budget ran out); game is server-dependent so a client archive alone would not make it playable.
games.why_interesting: A real 3D LEGO MMO with no official way to play, and a LEGO art style that suits low-poly Three.js.

games.name: Star Wars: Secrets of the Empire
games.how_lost: The VOID shut down in March 2020, and Disney ended its license, so the hardware-dependent experience has not run since.
games.revival_check: No home release; The VOID's IP passed to VR Exit LLC and a holding company, with no relaunch found; no emulation possible.
games.why_interesting: A high-profile Star Wars VR mission with many walk-through videos, though its physical props and haptics are hard to translate.

games.name: Mario Kart Arcade GP VR
games.how_lost: It was available primarily at Bandai Namco's VR Zone in Tokyo (plus a temporary 2018 London event) and was never released for home.
games.revival_check: No home release or dump. I could not confirm whether any VR Zone location still operates it (the search budget ran out), so it may still run somewhere.
games.why_interesting: A 4-player VR Mario Kart with item-grabbing hands, and kart racing is a natural fit for browser multiplayer.

games.name: Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Phantoms
games.how_lost: Ubisoft closed servers Dec 1, 2016, citing declining users.
games.revival_check: Fan 'Phantoms Forever' emulator had only login/master server and launcher per an undated post; no playable server found.
games.why_interesting: A free-to-play tactical cover shooter whose revival never got past login.

games.name: Fable Legends
games.how_lost: Cancelled during closed beta in 2016 when Lionhead closed, and servers went offline.
games.revival_check: An archivist (PtoPOnline) showed an offline build running in 2026; not publicly released. The 2027 Fable reboot is unrelated.
games.why_interesting: An asymmetric heroes-versus-villain design in a beloved world, preserved mostly as beta footage.

games.name: Dizzywood
games.how_lost: The studio closed it on December 31, 2010 for financial reasons, and SecretBuilders bought the assets.
games.revival_check: A fan project, Dizzywood: Rediscovered (started 2020), says it is in development but has no public release. Flashpoint not individually verified (search budget ran out); game is server-dependent so a client archive alone would not make it playable.
games.why_interesting: A 1.5M-player kids' world, and its assets are held by a company that never reused them.

games.name: Marvel Avengers Academy
games.how_lost: TinyCo shut the always-online game down in early 2019, alongside Spider-Man Unlimited.
games.revival_check: An itch.io fan remake ('Avengers Academy Re-Assembled') covers only the tutorial in v1.0.1. I found no private server.
games.why_interesting: A cult-favorite Marvel campus sim. A fan remake has started but is nowhere near complete.

games.name: Dissidia Final Fantasy Opera Omnia (Global)
games.how_lost: Square Enix ended global service on February 29, 2024 with no offline version, three chapters short of the story's end.
games.revival_check: There's no official offline mode. A fan named Hatok archived the cutscenes and battles on video. I found no private server. (The JP version had ended earlier.)
games.why_interesting: A huge Final Fantasy crossover whose story now survives only as video, which fits Argon's from-footage premise.

games.name: BarbieGirls.com
games.how_lost: Mattel closed BarbieGirls.com on June 1, 2011 and never reopened it.
games.revival_check: Mattel never announced a reopening. A fan project, Barbie Girls Rewritten, says it is recreating the world, but I could not verify whether it is playable. Flashpoint not individually verified (search budget ran out); game is server-dependent so a client archive alone would not make it playable.
games.why_interesting: A large mainstream kids' world, and footage of it is the main surviving record.

games.name: PlayStation Home
games.how_lost: Sony closed Home worldwide on March 31, 2015.
games.revival_check: The fan preservation project Destination Home reverse-engineered Home data (covered by IGN in 2021 and again about two years later). I could not confirm its current public-server state (the search budget ran out), and PSONE also lists Home as planned.
games.why_interesting: Its many small minigames and spaces survive mainly as footage, though it is UGC-adjacent and likely revived.

games.name: Catan: World Explorers
games.how_lost: Niantic pulled the early-access game from stores and shut the servers down on November 18, 2021.
games.revival_check: I found no revival or fan successor.
games.why_interesting: A rare attempt to turn Catan into a location-based MMO, though the footage is thin and the board game already exists.

games.name: Ghostbusters World
games.how_lost: The game closed on August 13, 2020 after weak player growth.
games.revival_check: I found no revival project.
games.why_interesting: An AR licensed game whose ghost-capture minigame could be rebuilt, though footage is likely limited.

games.name: Novus Prime (PlayStation Home)
games.how_lost: Became unplayable when Sony closed PlayStation Home worldwide on March 31, 2015.
games.revival_check: The fan project Destination Home is restoring Home (IGN covered it in 2021 and 2023 as 'playable'), but I could not confirm whether Novus Prime works in it, because the IGN fetch was blocked.
games.why_interesting: A small multiplayer space shooter that lived only inside a dead social platform. It is not strictly user-made, since a third-party studio built it.

games.name: Build-A-Bearville
games.how_lost: Build-A-Bear closed Bearville on March 31, 2015, and the replacement game it hinted at never shipped.
games.revival_check: A fan remake, Bearville Rewritten, was announced in November 2020 with a demo. Unofficial copies are also reported to exist. I could not verify how complete either is. Flashpoint not individually verified (search budget ran out); game is server-dependent so a client archive alone would not make it playable.
games.why_interesting: A tie-in world with known fan remake demand, and its unclear status makes it a borderline case.

games.name: The Club (Nickelodeon)
games.how_lost: Nickelodeon replaced Nicktropolis with The Club in May 2010, then closed it in stages through 2014-2016.
games.revival_check: No revival found. Lost Media Wiki says only a few screenshots and a commercial survive. Flashpoint not individually verified (search budget ran out); game is server-dependent so a client archive alone would not make it playable.
games.why_interesting: It is truly lost, but there is almost no footage, so it is a poor footage-based candidate.

games.name: Wii Karaoke U
games.how_lost: Singing required online-purchased tickets and streamed songs, and the service ended in Europe in 2017 and in Japan in 2023.
games.revival_check: Server-streamed content, with no Pretendo support found; no remake. Footage was not verified (the search budget ran out).
games.why_interesting: A pure service game in which everything lived on the server, but it fits Argon poorly.

games.name: Tabula Rasa
games.how_lost: NCsoft shut the MMO down in 2009.
games.revival_check: Infinite Rasa has a working dev server as of Oct 2026 but no public server; listing-site claims of live servers are unverified.
games.why_interesting: Richard Garriott's real-time-combat sci-fi MMO, a famous lost game.

games.name: Sodium / Sodium 2: Project Velocity (PlayStation Home)
games.how_lost: Went offline with the rest of PlayStation Home on March 31, 2015.
games.revival_check: Same as Novus Prime: Destination Home exists, but I could not verify whether the Sodium spaces function.
games.why_interesting: Home's first MMO-style game, with only two of its four planned parts released.

games.name: No Man's Land (PlayStation Home)
games.how_lost: Went offline when PlayStation Home closed on March 31, 2015.
games.revival_check: Destination Home fan revival exists, but I could not verify whether this game works in it.
games.why_interesting: A small team shooter that fits Argon's simple multiplayer, but footage is likely thin.

games.name: MAG
games.how_lost: Servers shut Jan 28, 2014, and the online-only game can no longer be played.
games.revival_check: PSONE fan servers revive many PS3 games; a 2022 WIP MAG server was not playable, and a PSONE review video title lists MAG as online again. Not verified; recheck.
games.why_interesting: Its 256-player battles were a technical landmark, with plenty of footage surviving.

games.name: Firefall
games.how_lost: Red 5 shut down servers with about 24 hours' notice in July 2017.
games.revival_check: The SINner / PIN emulator offers limited single-player exploration with no combat, AI, abilities or multiplayer.
games.why_interesting: A jetpack-driven open-world shooter MMO; the emulator lets you walk around but the game itself is gone.

games.name: Gunslinger Stratos 3
games.how_lost: Square Enix ended network service on April 1, 2021, and the PC version (Reloaded) closed in 2016.
games.revival_check: There is no home port, but a 'Teknoparrot' 4K gameplay video suggests the arcade build runs in TeknoParrot (likely offline only). The original online network is gone.
games.why_interesting: A fast 2v2 dual-pistol arena shooter that was hugely recorded in Japan.

games.name: Super Mario Bros. 35
games.how_lost: Nintendo pulled it on March 31, 2021, as a planned time-limited anniversary release.
games.revival_check: Kinnay's open-source server plus the 'Continued Interest' community server restore online play on modded Switches, with tournaments still held in 2025. | Kinnay's open-source SMB35 fan server works with patched (hacked) Switch consoles; turnout is low.
games.why_interesting: A strong concept, but already revived, so it is a filter-out reference.

games.name: Anthem
games.how_lost: EA shut down the always-online servers on January 12, 2026, leaving the game permanently unplayable.
games.revival_check: YouTuber And799 ran a local peer-to-peer proof of concept, described as an experiment and not a revival. Mark Darrah says private-server code exists, but nothing has been released. | Reports (Kotaku via Wikipedia) of a fan server or patch running days after shutdown; not independently verified.
games.why_interesting: A huge archive of footage exists for a recently lost AAA game, but its scale far exceeds a browser rebuild.

games.name: Concord
games.how_lost: Sony took the game offline and refunded players weeks after its August 2024 launch.
games.revival_check: A fan team rebuilt the backend in November 2025, and matches are playable but buggy on PC only. Sony issued copyright takedowns and invites were paused, so the revival is fragile and PS5 remains dead. | Fan custom servers restore matchmaking and a mode on PC (buggy, early); PS5 remains unplayable; reports of Sony takedowns.
games.why_interesting: One of the shortest-lived AAA games ever, but a fan revival exists, so filter it out.

games.name: Rumbleverse
games.how_lost: The official servers closed in February 2023.
games.revival_check: The fan mod rVclient restores login, parties and matchmaking on PC, and private-server hosting guides exist. | ProjectKO was shut down by takedown in 2024; successor rVclient mod and a community launcher restore play on PC.
games.why_interesting: Its wrestling-brawler battle royale suits a stylized rebuild, but it is revived on PC.

games.name: Spellbreak
games.how_lost: The servers were decommissioned in January 2023 after Blizzard acquired Proletariat.
games.revival_check: The developers released a free community version with a self-hostable server, and Elemental Fracture runs rebuilt accounts and matchmaking (PC only). | Developers released an official self-hostable Community Version on itch.io, with active fan servers.
games.why_interesting: Officially revived by its own developers, so it should be filtered out.

games.name: LawBreakers
games.how_lost: Nexon shut the servers down on September 14, 2018, after player counts collapsed.
games.revival_check: The fan RELB Project launcher ran public playtests in April 2024 with Cliff Bleszinski's blessing, though some modes were disabled. The PS4 version is still dead. | The RELB Project fan servers held public playtests in April 2024, endorsed by Cliff Bleszinski.
games.why_interesting: Its low-gravity arena movement is distinctive, but a PC revival exists.

games.name: Battleborn
games.platform: Windows, PS4, Xbox One (online-required, including single-player)
games.how_lost: The servers shut down on January 31, 2021, which locked out even the single-player campaign.
games.revival_check: The fan offline mod 'Reborn' restores the story campaign on Steam copies; there are no confirmed fan multiplayer servers, and consoles remain dead. | The 'Reborn' offline mod restores the story campaign on PC; PvP is unfinished.
games.why_interesting: It is a showcase case for games lost to server dependence, but partially revived.

games.name: Echo VR (Echo Arena / Echo Combat)
games.how_lost: Meta shut down the multiplayer servers on August 1, 2023.
games.revival_check: The EchoRelay mod by Xenomega restores online play on PC VR, and community servers such as the Echo VR Lounge run on it; Quest status is unclear. | EchoRelay fan relay and Echo VR Lounge community servers restore online play.
games.why_interesting: Its zero-g frisbee sport is a beloved VR esport and maps well to simple multiplayer, but it is revived on PC.

games.name: Planet Harriers
games.how_lost: It was a rare arcade-only Space Harrier sequel with no home port, long considered 'lost' in practice.
games.revival_check: The MAME set is a good dump but only preliminary emulation; a December 2025 DEmul update makes it playable start to finish.
games.why_interesting: A useful filter-out reference: a 'lost' arcade game that became emulatable in 2025.

games.name: Chromehounds
games.genre: Mech combat with persistent online war (Neroimus War)
games.how_lost: The online Neroimus War servers closed on January 6, 2010, leaving only the offline story mode.
games.revival_check: Wikipedia says the online servers were 'partly restored in May 2025 using Xenia Canary emulation', and the offline mode was always playable. | Since May 2025, fans have restored 6v6 online battles via Xenia Canary netplay; the war mode is still in progress.
games.why_interesting: Its persistent faction war between squads of custom mechs was the lost part, but it is now partly revived.

games.name: Marvel Heroes Omega
games.how_lost: Gazillion pulled it offline in Nov 2017.
games.revival_check: MHServerEmu reached v1.0.0 in March 2026, restoring the final build with community servers.
games.why_interesting: Fully emulated; exclude.

games.name: Dauntless
games.how_lost: Servers shut May 30, 2025.
games.revival_check: Dauntless Revived (fork of gwog's Undaunted) self-hosts the 1.4.4 (2020) client privately; later content is lost.
games.why_interesting: Old build revived; post-2020 content is lost.

games.name: Gundam Evolution
games.how_lost: Servers shut Nov 29, 2023.
games.revival_check: Side 7 private server public alpha since March 2024 (PC only).
games.why_interesting: Revived on PC.

games.name: The Cycle: Frontier
games.how_lost: Servers shut Sept 27, 2023.
games.revival_check: Two fan revival projects (including the Prospect emulator) and private servers advertised in 2026.
games.why_interesting: Revived by fans.

games.name: Nosgoth
games.how_lost: Square Enix shut the servers in 2016.
games.revival_check: Steam posts (2025-2026) describe a community private-server mod via Discord; no press verification.
games.why_interesting: Revived, though only community-verified.

games.name: Battlefield Heroes
games.how_lost: EA shut it down in mid-2015.
games.revival_check: Fan projects Rising Hub and Phoenix Heroes run revival servers.
games.why_interesting: Revived; exclude.

games.name: WildStar
games.how_lost: NCsoft shut down the MMO in Nov 2018.
games.revival_check: The NexusForever emulator supports the final build, but is incomplete and quests are not confirmed working.
games.why_interesting: Partially emulated.

games.name: Loadout
games.how_lost: Servers shut May 24, 2018, citing GDPR and server costs.
games.revival_check: The Loadout Reloaded fan project restores some multiplayer; sources disagree on how complete it is.
games.why_interesting: Partially revived.

games.name: Club Penguin Island
games.how_lost: Disney shut Club Penguin Island down in December 2018.
games.revival_check: OpenCPI (itch.io, April 2025) is a playable offline recreation on Windows, macOS and Linux. Waddle Penguins Island ran an online alpha in 2021, and CPI Remix targets 2026.
games.why_interesting: An iconic shutdown, but OpenCPI already makes it playable offline.

games.name: Mighty DOOM
games.how_lost: Microsoft closed the studio, and the servers shut down on August 7, 2024.
games.revival_check: A fan project, 'Mighty Resurrection', runs a recoded server (Korben, 2026).
games.why_interesting: A tight top-down roguelite, but it's playable again through a fan server.

games.name: Apex Legends Mobile
games.how_lost: EA discontinued Apex Legends Mobile in 2023.
games.revival_check: A paid, unverified private server built by Chinese players appeared in July 2026. Its safety and stability are disputed.
games.why_interesting: A huge battle royale. The revival is shaky, but it's too big for Argon anyway.

games.name: Minecraft Earth
games.how_lost: Microsoft shut it down on June 30, 2021.
games.revival_check: Project Genoa and Project Earth (Cloudburst plus GenoaPlugin) are fan server reimplementations, and a 'Revival Minecraft Earth' site uses Genoa. I didn't confirm a public hosted instance.
games.why_interesting: A major AR shutdown, but fan server code already exists.

games.name: NieR Re[in]carnation
games.how_lost: Square Enix ended service in 2024 with no offline version.
games.revival_check: Lunar Tear is a community server announced in April 2026 that makes the game partly playable. Users must supply their own client.
games.why_interesting: A notable NieR story game, but it's partly playable again.

games.name: The Simpsons: Tapped Out
games.how_lost: EA shut the servers down in January 2025.
games.revival_check: Fan servers Project Springfield (teamtsto.org, claims 25k+ players) and Tapped Out Reborn exist, and saved towns were archived.
games.why_interesting: A huge 13-year game, already revived by fans.

games.name: Pokémon Duel
games.how_lost: The official service ended in October 2018.
games.revival_check: Kaeru Team's 'Kaeru Duel' replacement server has been stable and free on Android since 2021.
games.why_interesting: A board-strategy game that would suit Argon well, but it's already revived.

games.name: Miitomo
games.how_lost: Nintendo ended service in May 2018.
games.revival_check: Kaeru Team's 'Kaerutomo' custom servers work on iOS and Android.
games.why_interesting: Nintendo's first mobile app, already revived.

games.name: Star Wars: Commander
games.how_lost: The servers shut down on June 12, 2020.
games.revival_check: The swcnoops private server on GitHub supports base attacks, and videos claim a 2023 'reboot' server. The revival is partial.
games.why_interesting: A Clash-style Star Wars base builder with a partial fan server.

games.name: Futurama: Worlds of Tomorrow
games.how_lost: The servers went offline on April 20, 2023, making it unplayable even offline.
games.revival_check: barncastle/FWOT-Server is a fan replacement API for client 1.5.7, and the CDNs still serve the assets. I couldn't verify whether it's maintained.
games.why_interesting: A licensed builder with a fan server, so it's low priority.

games.name: Survivor (Roblox)
games.how_lost: Content-deleted on September 17, 2020 after a DMCA claim from the TV show's rights holder.
games.revival_check: The original was deleted. The same team released Outlaster on Oct 9, 2020 with a similar format, which works as a rebranded spiritual successor, so this is marked revived for filtering.
games.why_interesting: Hugely popular social-deduction challenge game that suits simple multiplayer. IP issue: it copied CBS Survivor branding, which is why it was DMCA'd.

games.name: Project: Pokémon
games.how_lost: Deleted from Roblox around August 5, 2018 after a copyright strike tied to Nintendo/The Pokémon Company.
games.revival_check: The fan wiki says a community server re-uploads the game whenever it is taken down, and several fan remakes are distributed through Discord, so it is effectively revived in grey-market form.
games.why_interesting: One of the most famous Roblox takedowns. Major IP issue: it is entirely Pokémon IP, so it is unsuitable for rebuilding as-is.

games.name: Pokémon Brick Bronze
games.how_lost: Taken down from Roblox in 2018 over Pokémon copyright, along with other Pokémon games.
games.revival_check: Multiple fan revivals exist: Roria Unbound (website plus a Roblox re-upload), the Roria: Re-Awakened Discord, and Pokémon Reforged Bronze (a 2D remake).
games.why_interesting: The single best-known lost Roblox game. Major IP issue (Pokémon), and it already has revivals, so include it for reference only.

games.name: Booga Booga (original 2017)
games.how_lost: The original place (500M+ visits) was made private after its content rating was never updated, and the developer later quit.
games.revival_check: The original is private, but Soybeen uncopylocked and open-sourced it, and copies are playable, including 'BOOGA BOOGA - Classic' (games/4787629450) and a newer Booga Booga (games/11729688377).
games.why_interesting: An original-IP survival sandbox that fits Argon very well, though playable copies mean it is not truly lost.

games.name: Arcane Adventures
games.how_lost: Roblox's forced FilteringEnabled update broke the game (boats and core systems), and Vetex left it permanently broken.
games.revival_check: The Roblox page is titled [BROKEN] and says it is 'permanently broken', with no running servers. There is a fan recreation (Arcane Reborn, 2019), and Vetex's sequel Arcane Odyssey launched Feb 2023, so it is marked revived (remake and successor).
games.why_interesting: An original-IP Roblox RPG whose original version is unplayable, and the root of a major franchise.

games.name: Cowboys and Indians (The Hive Java)
games.how_lost: Dropped from The Hive before the Java network closed on April 15, 2021, and it was never ported to Hive Bedrock.
games.revival_check: The original is gone, but the community server KIG (mc.playkig.com, Aug 2024 listing) recreates CAI along with other Hive Java modes, so it is marked revived (fan recreation). There is also a 2020 Change.org petition to bring it back.
games.why_interesting: A team-objective mode that maps well onto simple multiplayer. The theme and name may need reworking for cultural sensitivity.

games.name: Gravity (The Hive Java)
games.how_lost: Went offline when The Hive shut down its Java Edition server on April 15, 2021.
games.revival_check: The eric.gg Hive page lists Gravity among the Java releases. The KIG community server says it recreates Gravity. I did not confirm whether Hive Bedrock has an equivalent.
games.why_interesting: A tiny, highly visual falling-course minigame and about the easiest possible rebuild for Argon.

games.name: Trouble in Mineville (The Hive Java)
games.how_lost: Went offline when The Hive closed its Java Edition network on April 15, 2021.
games.revival_check: The KIG community server recreates Trouble in Mineville (Aug 2024 listing). Hive Bedrock's Murder Mystery is a different game.
games.why_interesting: A hugely YouTubed Hive mode whose social-deduction loop is cheap to build and very fun with simple multiplayer.

games.name: Super Smash Mobs (Mineplex)
games.how_lost: Went offline when Mineplex shut down abruptly on May 11, 2023.
games.revival_check: Mineplex was bought by Samito (May 2023), ran closed betas in 2024 and 2025, and relaunched publicly on June 12, 2026, with Super Smash Mobs reportedly in the launch rotation.
games.why_interesting: An iconic Mineplex mode that has been revived, so it is included only so it can be filtered out.

games.name: Champions (Mineplex)
games.how_lost: Went offline when Mineplex shut down in May 2023.
games.revival_check: Champions appeared in the 2025 closed beta and is listed for the June 2026 public relaunch.
games.why_interesting: Revived, so it is included only for filtering.

games.name: FarmVille (original)
games.how_lost: Zynga shut it down on December 31, 2020, when Facebook dropped Flash.
games.revival_check: A fan preservation project, farmvillage, runs FarmVille 1 locally, and FV Replowed calls itself a revival. Flashpoint does not cover server games like this.
games.why_interesting: The defining Facebook game, but fan revivals exist.

games.name: Pixie Hollow (Disney Fairies online)
games.how_lost: Disney shut it down on September 19, 2013 to focus on mobile and Club Penguin.
games.revival_check: Several fan rebuilds exist: We the Pixies (alpha in 2023 with flight and two minigames), FairyABC, and Pixie Hollow Rewritten. None are official.
games.why_interesting: Flying 3D fairy hub worlds, with active fan remakes to compare against.

games.name: Wild Ones
games.how_lost: Playdom closed it on August 28, 2013.
games.revival_check: A fan remake, Wild Ones Remake, was released in May 2016, and a server-only revival project is on GitHub. Wild Ones: Private Wars was removed in 2017. I could not confirm the current status of either.
games.why_interesting: A small turn-based multiplayer artillery game, an ideal fit for Argon if the revivals turn out to be dead.

games.name: Monkey Quest
games.how_lost: Nickelodeon took the servers offline on September 26, 2014.
games.revival_check: MQReborn private server launched in September 2024 (4000+ community). An earlier Monkey Quest Reborn got a cease-and-desist in 2021.
games.why_interesting: A good 3D Unity kids' MMO, but a working private server now exists.

games.name: The World of Cars Online
games.how_lost: Disney closed it on February 8, 2012 after low paid membership.
games.revival_check: Sunrise Games remake was reported as nearly complete and launched a test server in July 2024.
games.why_interesting: A driving-based kids' world, but Sunrise Games has revived it.

games.name: Marvel Super Hero Squad Online
games.how_lost: Gazillion shut it down on January 11, 2017 and itself closed later that year.
games.revival_check: Fan revivals exist: SHSO Forever (retrosquadonline.com) and SHSU's reverse-engineered backend plus cached Unity files.
games.why_interesting: Popular Unity web MMO, but fan servers exist.

games.name: Battlestar Galactica Online
games.how_lost: Bigpoint shut down the official servers (I did not verify the date in this pass).
games.revival_check: Private server emulators exist (victti BSGO-Private-Server, OpenBSGO), plus community servers advertised in 2025.
games.why_interesting: A big 3D space MMO that has already been revived by fans.

games.name: Cartoon Network Universe: FusionFall
games.how_lost: Cartoon Network shut down the official servers, and fan server FusionFall Retro was itself closed after legal contact in 2020.
games.revival_check: OpenFusion (open-source server) and Retrobution are active in 2026.
games.why_interesting: An iconic Unity web MMO, already well revived by fans.

games.name: Free Realms
games.how_lost: SOE sunset the game, and only fan server emulators remain.
games.revival_check: OSFR Sanctuary open-source server emulator and launcher are on GitHub. I could not confirm a public server is running.
games.why_interesting: A big minigame-filled MMO, but an emulator exists.

games.name: Club Penguin
games.how_lost: Disney closed the official servers, and fan private servers took over.
games.revival_check: Club Penguin Journey and many other private servers (CPPS) are active in 2025-2026.
games.why_interesting: The archetypal kids' MMO, but thoroughly revived.

games.name: surviv.io
games.how_lost: Kongregate announced the shutdown on February 14, 2023, and servers became inaccessible around March 3, 2023.
games.revival_check: survev.io is an open-source near-complete recreation (2024). Suroi is a spiritual successor. resurviv was taken down by DMCA.
games.why_interesting: The best-known dead .io game, but survev.io already recreates it.

games.name: Stick Arena (Classic / Dimensions / Ballistick)
games.how_lost: XGen stopped hosting servers on November 30, 2022.
games.revival_check: Community private servers (BallistickEMU, Dimensions host) are listed as online in 2026.
games.why_interesting: A simple multiplayer Flash shooter, but private servers keep it alive.

games.name: Nicktropolis
games.how_lost: It went offline on March 9, 2010 (sources vary), and Nickelodeon later closed access to its file server.
games.revival_check: Nicktropolis Timewarp is an open-source fan rewrite built from screen-capture footage, with multiplayer and Ruffle minigames.
games.why_interesting: A precedent for Argon, since fans already rebuilt this game from footage alone.

games.name: Marvel: Avengers Alliance
games.how_lost: Playdom closed it on all platforms on September 30, 2016.
games.revival_check: MAA Redux is a fan offline rebuild from the original data (beta 6.18 in September 2025).
games.why_interesting: A hugely popular Facebook RPG, but already rebuilt by fans.

games.name: Restaurant City
games.how_lost: EA retired it on June 29, 2012.
games.revival_check: Restaurant City Reborn (rc-reborn.uk) runs the original client via Ruffle with a fan backend (GitHub Dippys/Restaurant-City-Server).
games.why_interesting: A beloved Playfish game, but now playable again.

games.name: Pet Society
games.how_lost: EA shut it down in June 2013.
games.revival_check: The mascotsociety server emulator runs locally, and an itch.io browser revival and the Paw Society rebuild are in progress.
games.why_interesting: A popular Playfish game, but there is a working emulator.

games.name: Glitch
games.how_lost: Tiny Speck shut the game down and donated nearly all its assets to the public domain.
games.revival_check: The fan revivals Eleven and Children of Ur merged in 2019, and Odd Giants is a separate Unity remake. Their release status is unclear.
games.why_interesting: Its public-domain assets make it legally clean, though fan revivals already exist.

games.name: Avatar: Legends of the Arena
games.how_lost: Nickelodeon stopped developing it and shut the servers (sources say around 2013).
games.revival_check: Fan servers (Legends Awakened and a classic server) are promoted in 2020 and 2026 videos. They are unofficial.
games.why_interesting: Arena bending combat fits session multiplayer, but fan servers exist.

games.name: UberStrike
games.how_lost: Cmune closed the servers in 2016 and the company itself closed in 2020.
games.revival_check: The Project Dropshot server emulator works with the Steam client, and Paradise Paintball 4D is a WebGL revival of its predecessor.
games.why_interesting: The definitive Unity Web Player FPS, but a fan emulator exists.
